{{Short description|None}}
[[File:Mike Keenan practice.PNG|thumb|Mike Keenan was the head coach of the Calgary Flames from 2007 to 2009.]]
The [[Calgary Flames]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Calgary]], [[Alberta]], Canada. The team is a member of the [[Pacific Division (NHL)|Pacific Division]] in the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). The Flames arrived in Calgary in 1980 after transferring from the city of [[Atlanta, Georgia]], where they were known as the [[Atlanta Flames]] from their founding in 1972 until relocation.<ref>{{cite book |title=2006–07 Calgary Flames Media Guide |publisher=Calgary Flames Hockey Club |editor=Hanlon, Peter |editor2=Kelso, Sean |page=4}}</ref>

[[Al MacNeil]] remained the Flames' coach when the franchise transferred to Calgary, serving as the team's first coach in Calgary. [[Bob Johnson (ice hockey b. 1931)|"Badger Bob" Johnson]], who succeeded MacNeil in 1982, is the Flames' all-time leader in games coached and wins.<ref>{{cite book |title=2007–08 Calgary Flames Media Guide |publisher=Calgary Flames Hockey Club}}</ref> He was behind the bench when the franchise made its first trip to the [[Stanley Cup Final]] in [[1986 Stanley Cup Final|1986]]. Johnson was elected to the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] in 1992, a year after his death from [[cancer]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMember.jsp?mem=b199202&type=Builder&page=bio&list=ByName#photo |title=The Legends – Bob Johnson |access-date=2008-09-16 |publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929110230/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMember.jsp?mem=b199202&type=Builder&page=bio&list=ByName#photo |archive-date=2007-09-29 }}</ref> Johnson's successor, [[Terry Crisp]], led the Flames to their only Stanley Cup championship in [[1989 Stanley Cup Playoffs|1989]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=12370 |title=Players – Terry Crisp |access-date=2008-09-16 |publisher=Hockey Hall of Fame |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071205155202/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/SearchPlayer.jsp?player=12370 |archive-date=2007-12-05 }}</ref>

The Flames went through several coaches between 1990 and 2003 as the team struggled to find playoff success. [[Doug Risebrough]], [[Dave King (ice hockey)|Dave King]], [[Pierre Page]], [[Brian Sutter]], [[Don Hay]] and [[Greg Gilbert]] all failed to lead the team past the first round as the Flames endured a 15-year period of playoff futility.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2004041922 |title=Recap: Calgary 3, Vancouver 2, OT |access-date=2008-09-17 |date=2004-04-20 |work=Yahoo! Sports |archive-date=2011-05-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110522195001/http://sports.yahoo.com/nhl/recap?gid=2004041922 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Darryl Sutter]] ended that streak in [[2003–04 NHL season|2003–04]] when he coached the Flames to a marked improvement over their previous season, ending with a trip to the [[2004 Stanley Cup Final]]. Though he did not win, Sutter earned a nomination for the [[Jack Adams Award]] as the league's top coach as a result of the team's performance.<ref>{{cite web |last=Roarke |first=Shawn P. |url=http://www.nhl.com/hockeyu/history/trophies/finalists042104.html |title=NHL announces awards finalists |access-date=2008-09-16 |date=2004-04-21 |website=National Hockey League |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060409050333/http://www.nhl.com/hockeyu/history/trophies/finalists042104.html |archive-date=2006-04-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Bob Hartley]] became the head coach in 2012 and won the 2015 Jack Adams Award. He was fired after the [[2015–16 NHL season|2015-16 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://flames.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=881171|title=Flames relieve Bob Hartley of coaching duties|website=flames.nhl.com|access-date=2016-06-17|archive-date=2016-08-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160814184932/http://flames.nhl.com/club/news.htm?id=881171|url-status=dead}}</ref> The current head coach of the Flames is [[Ryan Huska]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-name-ryan-huska-head-coach-344830986 |title=Flames Name Ryan Huska Head Coach |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 12, 2023 |date=June 12, 2023 |archive-date=June 12, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612175909/https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-name-ryan-huska-head-coach/c-344830986 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Notes==
* {{note label|Note1|A|A}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Flames. Thus, any coach who had two separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
* {{note label|Note1|B|B}} Before 1999, overtime losses were included in the loss column;<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Caldwell |first=Dave |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/17/sports/hockey/17score.html |title=Playing It Safe for a Bonus Point in the N.H.L. |access-date=2008-09-14 |date=2008-02-17 |journal=New York Times |archive-date=2016-01-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112104428/http://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/17/sports/hockey/17score.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Since 2005, ties are no longer possible.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Burnside |first=Scott |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/news/story?id=2114523 |title=Rule changes geared toward entertainment |access-date=2008-09-14 |date=2005-07-25 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=2016-02-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203193345/http://sports.espn.go.com/nhl/news/story?id=2114523 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* {{note label|Note1|C|C}} Does not include coaching record for the [[Atlanta Flames]].
* {{note label|Note1|D|D}} Charron served as interim coach for the remainder of the 1991–92 season following Risebrough's resignation.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wild.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tea_Risebrough |title=Doug Risebrough - President and General Manager |access-date=2008-09-16 |work=Minnesota Wild Hockey Club |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081006195537/http://wild.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tea_Risebrough |archive-date=2008-10-06 }}</ref>
* {{note label|Note1|E|E}} MacNeil served as interim head coach during the 2002–03 season following Gilbert's dismissal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/hockey/nhl/flames/2002-12-03-gilbert-fired_x.htm |title=Flames dump Gilbert, name MacNeil |access-date=2008-09-16 |date=2002-12-03 |work=USA Today | first=John | last=Marshall}}</ref>
* {{note label|Note1|F|F}} Ward served as interim head coach during the 2019–20 season following Peters' resignation. Ward also served as head coach for one game, a 3–2 overtime win over the [[Buffalo Sabres]], during the Flames' investigation into alleged misconduct by Peters during his previous coaching tenures. That win is reflected in Peters' totals.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/calgary/article/bill-peters-resigns-as-flames-bench-boss-geoff-ward-named-interim-coach/ |title=Bill Peters resigns as Flames bench boss, Geoff Ward named interim coach |access-date=2019-11-29 |date=2019-11-29 |work=CTV News |first=Ryan |last=White |archive-date=2019-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191129230922/https://calgary.ctvnews.ca/bill-peters-resigns-as-flames-bench-boss-geoff-ward-named-interim-coach-1.4708333 |url-status=live }}</ref>
* {{note label|Note1|G|G}} [[Ryan Huska]] served as interim head coach after Sutter's signing on March 4, 2021, who was unable to join the team due to the [[COVID-19]] protocol.<ref>{{cite web |title=Calgary Flames - Edmonton Oilers - March 6th, 2021 |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/cgy-vs-edm/2021/03/06/2020020383 |website=NHL.com |access-date=May 1, 2023 |date=March 6, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ottawa Senators - Calgary Flames - March 7th, 2021 |url=https://www.nhl.com/gamecenter/ott-vs-cgy/2021/03/07/2020020395 |website=NHL.com |access-date=May 1, 2023 |date=March 7, 2023}}</ref>
* {{note label|Note1|H|H}} Several years after his previous interim coaching stint, Huska was promoted to permanent head coach in June 2023, after Sutter was fired.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-name-ryan-huska-head-coach-344830986 |title=Flames Name Ryan Huska Head Coach |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 12, 2023 |date=June 12, 2023 |archive-date=June 12, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612175909/https://www.nhl.com/flames/news/flames-name-ryan-huska-head-coach/c-344830986 |url-status=live }}</ref>
